passages.title: Mindset 0 · Unit 9 — Multilingual: what it is like to speak many languages
passages.content:
You are going to read an article about a teenager who has a special skill.

1 Today, over 50% of the world's total population can speak more than one language. Maybe you are one of these people who can communicate in many languages. However, it may be unlikely that you can speak more than Richard Doner, an American teenager who can hold a conversation in over twenty languages.

2 Richard lives in New York. It is a city where there are people from hundreds of different countries. There are around 180 languages spoken in New York schools. This is why Richard believes that New York is the perfect city for him. 'I can discuss many different topics with people from all over the world and I don't even need to travel to another country,' Richard says.

3 Can he see a disadvantage? 'You can never rest. You have to continuously practise and put in lots of effort all the time to be able to remember the languages. I believe that, if your brain doesn't do any work, you can forget what you know. I don't have time to speak all of my languages every day, so if I want to get better, if I want to make progress, the important thing is that I speak each one as often as I can. If I don't, I start to forget the phrases and words that I know.'

4 He also believes that when you learn a language, you don't only learn words or phrases. 'A language helps you begin to learn more about the people and their cultures – their ideas, their food, what is important to them and so on.'

5 Richard is very popular all over the world. There are lots of videos online of him practising his skills in a wide range of languages, such as Arabic, Mandarin, German and even Swahili – a language that is common in West Africa.

6 The most important thing for Richard is to have fun when he learns a language. Learning is easier if you can make it interesting for yourself, he explains. 'Also, take your time – you have to learn at a speed that works for you.' I don't think many would disagree with him!

questionGroups.instruction: Read paragraphs 1–3 again. Choose the correct words to summarise the main ideas.

questions.questionText: Richard Doner is very special because he can speak ____ languages than most people.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: "hold a conversation in over twenty languages" → nhiều hơn hầu hết mọi người.

questions.questionText: Richard is very lucky as he has ____ opportunities to practise his language skills.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: New York có người từ hàng trăm quốc gia → rất nhiều cơ hội.

questions.questionText: Richard practises speaking each language ____ to improve.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: "I don't have time to speak all of my languages every day… I speak each one as often as I can" → regularly (không phải mỗi ngày).

questionGroups.instruction: Complete the sentences using NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the article.

questions.questionText: If Richard wants to talk with people from different countries, it isn't necessary to travel ____. (Paragraph 2)
questions.explanation: "I don't even need to travel to another country" → to another country.

questions.questionText: To remember languages, Richard makes sure his brain does ____. (Paragraph 3)
questions.explanation: "if your brain doesn't do any work, you can forget" → his brain does some work.

questions.questionText: If you know a language, you can start to understand about the people and ____. (Paragraph 4)
questions.explanation: "learn more about the people and their cultures".

questions.questionText: Swahili is a popular language in ____. (Paragraph 5)
questions.explanation: "Swahili – a language that is common in West Africa" (common = popular).

questions.questionText: When he learns a language, it is absolutely necessary for Richard to ____. (Paragraph 6)
questions.explanation: "The most important thing for Richard is to have fun".

sections.title: Mindset 0 · Unit 9 — Discussing a language project
sections.description: Sofia and Oliver plan a language project at an international college.
sections.transcript:
Sofia: Oliver, we need to discuss how to start our project. Remember that our teacher wants us to write the report on two things. One, how many students in college already speak more than one language…
Oliver: …yes, and two, what level their English is. It's a big project so I think we're going to have to speak to a lot of people.
Sofia: Yes, I know! Do you really think it'll be possible to speak to everyone? I'm not sure. There are over two hundred students in total.
Oliver: I know, but I guess only half of them speak just a single language.
Sofia: That's still a lot. I don't think we have enough time to go around and have a chat with the whole college. How are we going to show the results?
Oliver: I think it'll be a problem if we only include numbers. We need more than that.
Sofia: Yes, I agree. Maybe including some graphs or tables is a good idea. Let me think… First, we need to find out how many students we have here in the college in total. Then we can work out how many of them speak two or more languages.
Oliver: Can I make a suggestion? I think we can ask for that information from the college office first. I remember that, on my first day here, I put information about my second language on the registration form. So, I think it's the same for everyone.
Sofia: That's a good idea. That'll save us some time. I'll make an appointment to go and speak to somebody there after class. Who do I need to see? Is it Miss Wainwright?
Oliver: No, she works in the student services room. You need to see Miss Smith. She's in the college office.
Sofia: Can you remind me where that is? Is it next door to the IT services offices where Mr Black works?
Oliver: No, Mr Black is in the student administration office so you need to go to the floor above.
Sofia: Oh, OK. I know where that is now.
Oliver: Great. OK, I'm going to have lunch. Do you want to join me?
Sofia: No, sorry, I can't. I need to study for my maths test. Enjoy your lunch. I'm going to study in the library. Bye!

questionGroups.instruction: Listen to Sofia and Oliver. Decide whether these sentences are True or False.

questions.questionText: There are over 200 students in the school who speak more than one language.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Có hơn 200 học sinh trong trường nói được hơn một ngôn ngữ.

Vị trí: Đầu bài.

Transcript: “There are over two hundred students in total” … “I guess only half of them speak just a single language”

Phân tích: 200 là TỔNG số học sinh, không phải số người nói nhiều thứ tiếng → False.

questions.questionText: Oliver thinks that they shouldn't only include numbers in the report.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Oliver nghĩ không nên chỉ đưa con số vào báo cáo.

Vị trí: Giữa bài.

Transcript: “I think it'll be a problem if we only include numbers. We need more than that”

Phân tích: True.

questions.questionText: Oliver can speak more than one language.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Oliver nói được hơn một ngôn ngữ.

Vị trí: Khi Oliver đưa ra gợi ý.

Transcript: “I put information about my second language on the registration form”

Phân tích: Có ngôn ngữ thứ hai → True.

questionGroups.instruction: Listen again and complete the table. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer.

questions.explanation:
Dịch: Phòng của Miss Wainwright

Vị trí: Khi Sofia hỏi cần gặp ai.

Transcript: “No, she works in the student services room”

Phân tích: student services.

Dịch: Phòng của Miss Smith

Vị trí: Ngay sau đó.

Transcript: “You need to see Miss Smith. She's in the college office”

Phân tích: college office.

Dịch: Phòng của Mr Black

Vị trí: Gần cuối.

Transcript: “Is it next door to the IT services offices where Mr Black works?” … “No, Mr Black is in the student administration office”

Phân tích: BẪY: IT services là ý sai của Sofia → student administration office.

questions.questionText: Where is Sofia going to next?
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Sofia sẽ đi đâu tiếp theo?

Vị trí: Câu cuối.

Transcript: “I need to study for my maths test” … “I'm going to study in the library”

Phân tích: Ôn thi toán (không phải lớp toán) ở thư viện; Oliver mới đi ăn trưa → A.
